History of Hamas.fact: October 2004 – Killing of Adnan al-Ghoul, assistant of Mohammed Deif, the leader of the Izz ad-Din al-Qassam brigades.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: 11 November 2004 – Death of _____, chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and president of the Palestinian National Authority
History of Hamas.fact: 11 November 2004 – Death of Yasser Arafat, chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and president of the Palestinian National Authority. PLO chairman Mahmoud Abbas elected to replace Yasser Arafat.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: January 2005 _____ presidential election – Hamas boycotts them
History of Hamas.fact: 11 November 2004 – Death of Yasser Arafat, chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and president of the Palestinian National Authority. January 2005 Palestinian presidential election – Hamas boycotts them.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: 25 _____ 2006 – Victory of the Hamas at the legislative election, which took 74 seats of the 132 seats
History of Hamas.fact: Palestinian municipal elections, January–May 2005 – Relative success of Hamas, which took control of Beit Lahia in northern Gaza, Qalqilyah in the West Bank and Rafah. 25 January 2006 – Victory of the Hamas at the legislative election, which took 74 seats of the 132 seats.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: March 2007 – _____ established a national unity government headed by Ismail Haniyeh
History of Hamas.fact: March 2007 – The Palestinian Legislative Council set up a national unity government headed by Ismail Haniyeh.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: June 2007 – Hamas begins a takeover of _____, ending the coalition with Fatah
History of Hamas.fact: June 2007 – Hamas begins a takeover of Gaza, ending the coalition with Fatah. 16 October 2024 – New Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was killed in combat in Gaza with the Israeli military April 2025 – Yahya Fathi Abd al-Qader Abu Shaar, the head of Hamas' weapons smuggling network, was killed by Israeli army.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: 31 July 2024 – _____ military chief of Hamas, Mohammed Deif, was killed by Israel 's military
History of Hamas.fact: 31 July 2024 – Senior military chief of Hamas, Mohammed Deif, was killed by Israel 's military.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: 31 July 2024 – Hamas leader, _____ was killed in Iran
History of Hamas.fact: March 2007 – The Palestinian Legislative Council set up a national unity government headed by Ismail Haniyeh. 31 July 2024 – Hamas leader, Ismail Haniyeh was killed in Iran.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: May 2025 – _____, Hamas leader in Gaza and the brother of Yahya Sinwar, was allegedly killed by Israeli airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip
History of Hamas.fact: May 2025 – Mohammed Sinwar, Hamas leader in Gaza and the brother of Yahya Sinwar, was allegedly killed by Israeli airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: 30 August 2025 – _____, the spokesman for Hamas' armed wing, was killed by Israeli military
History of Hamas.fact: 30 August 2025 – Abu Obaida, the spokesman for Hamas' armed wing, was killed by Israeli military.

History of Hamas.question: 26 May 2026, _____, successor of al-Haddad, was killed in an Israeli strike
History of Hamas.fact: 26 May 2026, Mohammed Odeh, successor of al-Haddad, was killed in an Israeli strike.

History of Hamas.subject: International Relations
History of Hamas.question: On 13 _____ 2025, Israel's assassination killed senior commander Ra'ad Sa'ad (Raed Saed), who was described as the second-in-command of the Hamas's armed wing
History of Hamas.fact: On 13 December 2025, Israel's assassination killed senior commander Ra'ad Sa'ad (Raed Saed), who was described as the second-in-command of the Hamas's armed wing.
